methods.detail: Use the district's online filing system if it has one, and keep the confirmation.
Mail the protest so it is postmarked on or before the last day (Tax Code §1.08); use a method that gives a dated receipt.
Deliver the protest to the district office and ask for a dated copy.

hearing_documents: Your written request for the district's evidence, with proof of the date you sent it
notes: Ask the chief appraiser in writing for the district's evidence when you file. Information you request that is not delivered at least 14 days before the hearing cannot be used by the district (Tax Code §41.461; §41.67(d)).

legal_basis.protest_form: Form 50-132, Property Owner's Notice of Protest (the form is optional; counties under 120,000 population use Form 50-132-A)

tax_rates.source: Sample tax rate sheet for the Exampleville taxing units

eligible.name: Over-65 or disabled additional school exemption
eligible.how_to_claim: The district must grant it without an application if your birth date is already in its records and you have the general homestead exemption. Otherwise file Form 50-114 with the appraisal district (not the Comptroller) with a copy of your Texas driver's license or state ID showing the property address. Apply no later than the first anniversary of turning 65.
documents: Texas driver's license or state ID showing the property address
eligible.note: Effective January 1 of the tax year you turn 65 and applies to the whole year. An owner who is both 65 or older and disabled may choose either exemption, not both.

eligible.name: School tax ceiling (tax freeze)
eligible.how_to_claim: There is no separate application: the ceiling follows the over-65 or disabled school exemption. Ask the school district's tax office for the dollar ceiling that applies to your account.
eligible.note: Savings depend on future rate and value changes, so they are not included in the estimate.
